recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit as-is. No core FHIR follow-up is needed for FHIR-22738 unless a later Patient Care decision changes AdverseEvent patient search semantics beyond the already-present Patient-targeted parameter.
issue_request: FHIR-22738 was a Published/Persuasive Patient Care change request for FHIR-core AdverseEvent, applied for R5, asking to add search parameters for patient and identifier.
initial_application: The Jira comment identifies 2019-07-11 commit 8f2524d6e1f36cfd6ef0eca8cceedc2b4b39f959 as the pre-application; that commit added patient/reference and identifier/token rows to source/adverseevent/adverseevent-spreadsheet.xml.
additional_context: AdverseEvent is still active in source/fhir.ini, and the 2021 source refactor commit 33b409a4b6d544598262f2f074ebb4b6dc466157 replaced the spreadsheet with the current XML structuredefinition and search-parameter bundle. The same pre-application commit also mentioned FHIR-22736, but that issue concerned AdverseEvent code-system code casing, not this search-parameter request. Zulip and Confluence searches found no relevant community evidence changing the conclusion.
reconciliation: No source files were changed. source/adverseevent/bundle-AdverseEvent-search-params.xml already defines AdverseEvent-identifier with code identifier, type token, and expression AdverseEvent.identifier, and AdverseEvent-patient with code patient, type reference, expression AdverseEvent.subject.where(resolve() is Patient), and target Patient.
